decisions.question: Is adding sealed MultiWriterTopic<T> between Topic<T> and EventTopic<T>/ReplayTopic<T> a compatible amendment of topic-model@v1, or a breaking one that needs v2 (and so a run stop)?

options.label: amend v1 compatibly
options.consequence: Keeps topic-model@v1; bus-api@v1's Interface and fixtures compile as written. Accepts one changed inference result (the least upper bound of an event and a replay topic) as outside the declared surface.

options.label: draft topic-model@v2
options.consequence: Treats the inference change as breaking: a v2 with a migration note for a draft contract with no producer or consumer code, and every consumer contract re-pointed at v2.

options.label: report a breaking-amend run stop
options.consequence: Ends the run until the owner rules on whether an inference-only change counts as breaking.

decisions.why: The experiment replays every topic-model@v1 fixture as it stood at df5e8f8 against a stand-in carrying the amendment: structure, surface, reject and all 40 behavior cases pass (A1 to A4), exactly as against the stand-in without it (D1). topology-dsl@v1's and topology-ir@v1's surface and reject sets, and topology-dsl@v1's recorder suite, give identical results against both stand-ins (C1, C2, D3). No leaf variant is added, so the three-variant exhaustive switch in the existing surface and G1's non-exhaustive reject keep their results; seeded defect M1 shows that this holds only because the intermediate is sealed (an abstract one makes the existing three-variant switch non-exhaustive). One source-level effect exists and is recorded in the contract's Versioning: the least upper bound of EventTopic<int> and ReplayTopic<int> moves from Topic<int> to MultiWriterTopic<int>, so `final mixed = [event, replay]; mixed.add(state);` compiles before and fails after (probe/lub.dart, C3 against D4). That is the same class of edge the Versioning section already accepts as compatible (a new top-level function can collide with a consumer's import; a new getter can shadow a consumer's extension member), it touches no type the Interface states, no consumer code exists (every contract is draft, no package exists), and no existing fixture hits it. Signal that would have changed my mind: a consumer fixture or contract text that relies on the inferred type of such a mix, or the contract being stable with code already built against it.
evidence: hsdd/contract/topic-model.md ## Versioning (pre-existing Breaking and Compatible lists)

decisions.question: Which guarantee carries which part of the MultiWriterTopic rule?

options.label: extend G1, add G27 for assignability
options.consequence: G1 keeps describing the closed family exactly (MultiWriterTopic sealed, its subtypes exactly EventTopic and ReplayTopic, switches over it exhaustive); G27 holds the new rule bus-api@v1 depends on: a StateTopic, or a Topic of statically unknown variant, is not a MultiWriterTopic, and `is MultiWriterTopic` holds exactly for event and replay topics.

options.label: leave G1, put everything in G27
options.consequence: G1 would no longer describe the family exactly: a sealed member of it would go unmentioned, and closedness would be split across two ids.

options.label: fold the rule into G2
options.consequence: G2 is about members only a state topic has; mixing in the converse assignability rule blurs what a G2 reject failure means.

decisions.chosen: extend G1, add G27 for assignability
decisions.why: G1's subject is closedness, which now includes MultiWriterTopic; extending its statement keeps the id (ADR-001 item 3) and every pre-existing G1 fixture still passes (A3). The assignability rule is new behavior that bus-api@v1 G11 and G19 cite, so it gets its own id for --guarantee restrictions. No evidence beyond the brief and ADR-001 item 3 was needed; the choice is about where a reader looks.

decisions.question: How is G27 covered, and where do G1's new cases go?

options.label: reject file plus behavior case and surface uses, G1 cases appended to its file
options.consequence: A new reject library for G27 (state topic by explicit and by inferred type argument, an unnarrowed Topic, an assignment, a set element), one behavior case for the run-time `is` and pattern result, surface uses of every MultiWriterTopic form; G1's two new cases appended to topic_family_is_closed.dart so its existing markers keep their lines.

options.label: reject file only, new file for G1's cases
options.consequence: Leaves the run-time hierarchy unpinned, although bus-api@v1's live binding matches `case MultiWriterTopic<T>()` at run time, and splits one guarantee across two reject libraries against ADR-001 item 4.

decisions.chosen: reject file plus behavior case and surface uses, G1 cases appended to its file
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 4 wants one reject library per type-level guarantee and surface libraries that use every declaration. The behavior case is cheap and pins what a pattern-matching consumer relies on (hsdd/contract/fixture/bus-api/behavior/bus_activation_test.dart matches on MultiWriterTopic). Every code was confirmed in the probe before the fixtures were written (P1), and seeded defects M1 and M2 show the new cases fail when the rule breaks.

decisions.question: Fold in S07's note: state the lineage a state topic's initial value carries when it is first observed or read? If so, which lineage?

options.label: add it now as Lineage.root() with defaults
options.consequence: Matches topology-dsl@v1's read row word for word; the initial value starts a new flow when it leads to a publish and is not sensitive in its lineage, while the published envelope still carries its topic's flag (G14).

options.label: add it as Lineage.root(sensitive: topic.sensitive)
options.consequence: Propagates a sensitive topic's flag into the lineage of its initial value, but contradicts topology-dsl@v1's read row, which would need its own amendment, and diverges from how the contract already treats a Tracing.disabled read.

options.label: leave it for a later touch
options.consequence: topic-model@v1's 'How the lineage functions are applied' paragraph keeps omitting a case its consumer states, so the two contracts read differently.

decisions.chosen: add it now as Lineage.root() with defaults
decisions.why: The Specification is silent on the lineage of an initial value (Spec §2.5 seeds the subject, Spec §3.5 speaks of envelopes, and an initial value has none). topology-dsl@v1's read row already applies Lineage.root() to it, so stating it here fills a gap without changing any function, default or rule. The sensitive variant buys nothing observable: G14 makes every published envelope carry its topic's flag, and the lineage flag reaches only a raw operator's PipelineValue. Correction to the brief: bus-api@v1 does not state this lineage itself; it inherits it through topology-dsl@v1's live semantics. Signal that would have changed my mind: a consumer that reads Lineage.sensitive, for example a diagnostic that redacts by lineage, which would favor root(sensitive: topic.sensitive) here and for Tracing.disabled reads alike.

decisions.question: How does ## Versioning record the amendment?

options.label: amendment line plus a new Compatible class
options.consequence: Records this amendment, its evidence and the inference change, and adds 'a new sealed type between Topic and existing variants that adds no variant' to the Compatible list, with the abstract-intermediate caveat, so the next such change need not be re-derived.

options.label: amendment line only
options.consequence: Records this amendment, but leaves the general rule implicit in one history line.

decisions.chosen: amendment line plus a new Compatible class
decisions.why: The Breaking list names 'retyping any declaration' and 'adding a variant'; a reader could take a variant's new supertype as a retype. Naming the class, with M1's finding that only a sealed intermediate qualifies, settles that for future edits.

experiments.question: Is the MultiWriterTopic amendment compatible within topic-model@v1: do the fixtures written before it, and the consumers' fixtures, keep their results against an implementation carrying it; which codes do the new reject cases report; do the new fixtures actually depend on the amendment; what changes for inference?
experiments.finding: Against the amended stand-in, the topic-model@v1 fixtures at df5e8f8 pass every set (structure 26/26, surface clean, 9 reject files, 40 behavior cases), the amended fixtures pass every set (27/27, 10 reject files, 41 cases), topology-dsl@v1 and topology-ir@v1 surface and reject sets pass as they do without the amendment, bus-api@v1's surface and reject sets pass, and the bus-api suite (86) and topology-dsl@v1's live suite (43) pass. Without the amendment the new topic-model surface and the two changed reject files fail, and bus-api@v1's two publish reject files fail. Seeded defects: MultiWriterTopic abstract instead of sealed fails G1's reject and surface, including the pre-existing three-variant switch; StateTopic as a MultiWriterTopic fails G27's reject and behavior case. Inference: the least upper bound of an event and a replay topic changes from Topic<T> to MultiWriterTopic<T>, so a variable or list inferred from those two alone rejects a later state topic (probe/lub.dart: no diagnostic before, two errors after).
